```markdown
# Incident Postmortem: Database Connection Pool Exhaustion

## Summary
**Severity:** P1 | **Duration:** 4h 23m | **Date:** 2026-11-06  
API service degradation → unavailability. Root cause: downstream payment service responding in 45–180s instead of <5s, exhausting connection pool, cascading to user-facing timeouts.

## Impact
- 4h 23m: API returning 503 errors
- ~18k requests failed
- Revenue impact: $40k (unprocessed transactions)
- ~8k users experienced "service unavailable" errors

---

## Timeline

| Time | Event |
|------|-------|
| 14:32 | Payment service starts experiencing latency (internal monitoring gap—not visible to us) |
| 14:47 | First alerts: API p99 latency 45s (noise threshold, ignored) |
| 14:58 | Second wave of slow payment responses. Pool exhaustion begins |
| 15:03 | Alert: 50% error rate. On-call paged |
| 15:05 | Oncall confirms API is down; starts investigation |
| 15:12 | Payment team contacted; they confirm their service is degraded (network issue upstream of them) |
| 15:20 | Mitigation: circuit breaker added, payment requests fail-fast (graceful degradation) |
| 15:22 | API recovers; transaction queue builds, manual retry process started |
| 15:45 | Payment service recovers fully |
| 16:00 | API back to normal; all queued transactions processing |
| 18:55 | All manual retries complete; service stable |

---

## Root Cause

**Primary:** Connection pool exhaustion  
Payment service responses jumped from 2–5s to 45–180s due to upstream network saturation (their CDN provider). Our HTTP client had no explicit timeout; requests hung indefinitely in the pool. With 50 pool connections, exhaustion → queue → cascading 503s to end users.

**Why not caught earlier:**
- No circuit breaker on payment calls
- No per-request timeout (only socket timeout, ignored by hanging connections)
- No monitoring of pool utilization (only success/error metrics)
- Latency alerts only trigger on >60s (p99 hit 45s, below threshold)

---

## Remediations

### Immediate (done during incident)
- ✅ Deploy circuit breaker: fail fast after 2 consecutive 30s timeouts on payment calls

### Short-term (48h)
- ✅ Set HTTP request timeout to 10s (was infinite)
- ✅ Add connection pool utilization metric + alert at 70% usage
- ✅ Lower latency alert threshold from 60s to 15s

### Medium-term (2 weeks)
- [ ] Implement bulkhead pattern: separate pool for external payment calls (10 connections, don't starve internal queries)
- [ ] Add downstream SLA monitoring: track payment service p50/p95/p99 and alert if p95 > 8s
- [ ] Implement request-level timeout with jitter for retries

### Long-term (roadmap)
- [ ] Migrate to async payment processing (decouple from critical path)
- [ ] Vendor payment service with SLA penalty clause; formalize escalation
- [ ] Load-test pool exhaustion scenarios quarterly

---

## Detection Gaps

| Gap | Should have caught at | How |
|-----|---|---|
| Slow downstream service | T+5m | Monitor payment service response times directly; alert at p95 >8s |
| Pool exhaustion | T+2m | Expose `hikari_connections_active` metric; graph + alert >35/50 |
| Cascading failure | T+3m | Circuit breaker on external calls; fail fast instead of hanging |

---

## Action Items

| Owner | Task | Due | Priority |
|-------|------|-----|----------|
| On-call | Deploy circuit breaker | Done | P0 |
| SRE | Add pool monitoring dashboard | 2026-11-07 | P0 |
| Backend | Add request timeout | 2026-11-07 | P0 |
| Backend | Bulkhead pattern (separate pool) | 2026-11-13 | P1 |
| Platform | Payment SLA monitoring | 2026-11-13 | P1 |
| PM/Eng | Vendor payment contract review | 2026-11-20 | P2 |

---

## What Went Well
- Alert firing correctly (despite threshold being too high)
- Oncall diagnosed pool exhaustion in <10m
- Circuit breaker deployed and working immediately
- Clear communication with payment team

## What We'll Do Differently
- External dependency timeouts are *not optional*—enforce at code review
- Pool metrics as mandatory observability, not optional
- Circuit breaker now a standard library for any external HTTP calls
- Quarterly chaos tests on pool exhaustion + downstream latency
```
